target.title: fix(chutes): validate OAuth redirect URI port is in range 1-65535
target.body:
## Description

The Chutes OAuth redirect URI parser (`parseRedirectUri`) and the deprecated `waitForLocalCallback` command path both parse a user-supplied `redirect_uri` port via `Number.parseInt(url.port, 10)` without validating that the result falls within the valid TCP port range (1-65535). Port 0 and values above 65535 could produce unexpected behavior when passed to the local HTTP server.

This PR adds an explicit port bounds check (1-65535) and rejects invalid ports with a clear error message.

**Files changed:**
- `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts` — add port bounds validation in `parseRedirectUri`, export the function for testability
- `extensions/chutes/oauth.test.ts` — 6 test cases covering: default port, valid port, upper bound (65535), lower bound (1), port 0 rejection, port >65535 rejection
- `src/commands/chutes-oauth.ts` — apply the same bounds check to the deprecated command-line OAuth path

## Related Issue

N/A (self-contained improvement)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change)

## Testing

### Unit tests

```
✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > accepts default port 80 when no port is specified
✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > accepts valid port in range 1-65535
✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > accepts port 65535 (upper bound)
✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > accepts port 1 (lower bound)
✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > rejects port 0
✓ parseRedirectUri port bounds > rejects port above 65535
```

All 6 new tests pass. Existing Chutes OAuth tests (bounded JSON response, login flow) continue to pass.

### Negative control

Before the fix, `parseRedirectUri("http://127.0.0.1:0/callback")` would return `{ port: 0 }` without error. After the fix, it throws `Chutes OAuth redirect URI port must be 1-65535 (got 0)`.
